content.text:
Done. All three PNGs are rendered from a single `flyer.html` driven by a `?s=` scale parameter.

**Deliverables** (in the working folder):
- `portrait.png` — 1080×1350, scale 1 (master)
- `wide.png` — 1200×1000, scale 0.85
- `sky.png` — 300×600, scale 0.28

**How it holds up across sizes**
- Every dimension (type, icons, badges, padding, gaps) is `calc(px * var(--s))`, so content scales exactly 1 / 0.85 / 0.28.
- Body is a flex column with flexible spacer elements, so leftover height distributes evenly instead of leaving dead space or overflowing — that's why the sky skyscraper (which has ~220px of slack) stays balanced and the wide format (which is naturally too tall) still fits.
- The photo band and CTA bar are edge-to-edge at all three sizes; only inner sections carry side padding. The photo uses `object-fit: cover` with a `min()`-capped height, so it crops (never distorts) — 1080×540, 1200×400, 300×157.
- Candidates are a 3-column `1fr` grid, so columns stay evenly spaced at every width (verified sky centers at 59.5 / 150 / 240.5 with 37–41px of clearance between names).
- Steps stack vertically in portrait/sky but flip to a single row in landscape (`min-aspect-ratio: 1/1`), which reclaims the height the wide format needed; `space-between` with auto-width items keeps each step on one line instead of one awkwardly wrapping.

**Verification**: I measured every element's box in-page at all three sizes — `scrollHeight === clientHeight` and no horizontal overflow for each, zero elements with clipped content, and consistent top/bottom padding (34px portrait, 29px wide, 31px sky). I also inspected a 3× sky render to confirm the small text is clean and nothing overlaps. One defect found and fixed along the way: the wide format initially had a 480px photo squeezing the margins to ~10px and wrapping the first step onto two lines.
